name: קיצון מוחלט על משולש סגור (באנגלית)
questiontext:
Consider the function g(x,y)={{CT:0}} and the points

\[ A={{CT:1}}, B={{CT:2}}, C={{CT:3}} \]

Find the absolute maximum and minimum values of \(g(x,y)\) on the (closed) triangle \(\triangle ABC\) whose vertices are \(A,B,C\).

Max: [[input:ans1]]
[[validation:ans1]]
Min: [[input:ans2]]
[[validation:ans2]]
generalfeedback:
Outline: The absolute extrema of a differentiable function on a closed triangle are attained at interior critical points or on the boundary. Find the critical point, reduce \(g\) on each edge to a function of one variable, and compare all candidate values.
Step 1 — Where the extrema can be
Since the function is differentiable the maximum and minimum can be obtained either on the boundary of the triangle (consisting of three edges and three vertices) or in critical points. 
Step 2 — The critical point
Critical points occur where the gradient vanishes \(\nabla g(x,y)={{CT:4}} =\overline{0}\). Solving this linear equation we see that the gradient vanishes at one point \(p = {{CT:5}}\). This point is {{CT:6}}.
Step 3 — The edges
Now let us consider the edges of the triangle. For example let us look for maximum and minimum of the function restricted to the edge \(BC\). This can be done using calculus of functions of one variable, by expressing the restriction of our function to this edge as a function of one variable, say \(x\). On this edge \(y={{CT:7}}\) so substituting and simplifying we obtain \(g(x,{{CT:7}})={{CT:8}}\). We are interested in this function on the interval \([{{CT:9}},{{CT:10}}]\). This function has one critical point at \(x = {{CT:11}}\). The corresponding point on the edge \(BC\) is \({{CT:12}}\) and the value of the function there is \({{CT:13}}\). The values of the function on the edge of the interval correspond of course to the values of the original function on the points \(B\) and \(C\) respectively. 

Carrying out a similar analysis for the other two edges we obtain six different points that we have to consider. One critical point on each edge and the three vertices. Yielding 

\[g({{CT:12}})={{CT:13}}, g({{CT:14}})={{CT:15}}, g({{CT:16}})={{CT:17}}\]

\[g(A)={{CT:18}}, g(B)={{CT:19}}, g(C)={{CT:20}}\]

[[if test="{{CT:24}}"]]

The critical point \(p={{CT:5}}\) lies inside the triangle, so it is a seventh candidate:

\[g(p)={{CT:21}}\]

[[/if]]
Step 4 — Comparing the values
Taking the maximum and minimum over the value of the function on these [[if test="{{CT:24}}"]]seven[[else]]six[[/if]] points we obtain

\[ \max g={{CT:22}},\qquad \min g={{CT:23}} \]
